findings.description: The synchronous wrapper gives the copy the previous thread-local statistics dictionary instead of the dictionary exposed by `wrapped_f.statistics`. Statistics from the first call are therefore never published on the decorated function.
findings.rationale: On the first invocation of a decorated synchronous function, `self._local.statistics` and the wrapper's initial statistics dictionary are distinct objects. This assignment makes the retry execution update the former, while line 379 exposes the latter, which remains empty. Users reading the function's statistics after that call receive no results, including through additional decorators.

findings.description: Concurrent invocations now mutate the same statistics dictionary, so their statistics overwrite and accumulate into each other.
findings.rationale: When two tasks call the same async decorated function concurrently, both retry copies receive `async_wrapped.statistics`. Starting the second invocation clears the first invocation's statistics, and subsequent retries update shared counters. For example, if both invocations fail once and then succeed, the shared attempt counter can reach three although neither invocation made three attempts. Previously each invocation's copy maintained its own dictionary.
